title: Tiered contextual fallback controller: per-entity breakers, trip profiles, and safe degraded outputs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a Tiered Contextual Fallback Controller (TCFC) that provides per-tenant/per-model/per-dependency circuit breakers with graded trip thresholds, hysteresis, and safe fallback behaviors across regions. The controller should enable deterministic and probabilistic shedding strategies, map tripped requests to compatible model-variants or cached K/V prefix responses, and coordinate multi-region failover with SLO-aware routing decisions. This ticket covers design, implementation, simulation, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: [1] Controller exposes per-entity configuration API (tenant/model/dependency) and default global profile. [2] Simulated load tests show SLO preservation (P95 latency and availability) under 3 synthetic failure modes with at least 2 partner tenants. [3] Fallback mappings return safe degraded outputs (cached response, short stub, or lower-capacity model) that maintain schema compatibility. [4] Multi-region failover triggers within configured latency SLO windows and does not produce request duplication. [5] Feature flags and observability (dashboards, perf traces, Spike detectors) present for canary rollout.
technical_notes: Key concepts: (a) Trip profiles - combine rate, error-rate, latency quantiles, and model queue length into a monotonic risk score; thresholds defined as soft/hard bands. (b) Hysteresis - two-stage cool-down windows (soft open -> probation -> fully closed) to avoid flapping. (c) Graded shedding - map risk score ranges to actions: 0=no-op, 1=slow-path (smaller batch/longer timeout), 2=prefer cheaper model variant, 3=serve cached/approximate response, 4=reject-with-grace (HTTP 503 + retry-after + fallback payload). (d) Probabilistic sample-based shedding for bursty tenants to avoid sharp cutoff. (e) KV-cache warm-fallback - prioritize prefix cache where applicable, with TTL and quality penalty. (f) Multi-region coordination - prefer local region; escalate to paired region only when local region's risk score exceeds configurable region-trip threshold. (g) Telemetry - emit risk_score, trip_state, reason_tags, fallback_type, and an idempotency token for cross-region dedup. Trade-offs: stronger isolation for tenants increases config surface and memory usage; probabilistic shedding improves fairness but complicates reproducibility.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit tests + integration harness in staging (week 1). Phase 1: Canary in eu-west with low-traffic tenant group, feature-flagged behavior, 48h burn-in and synthetic spike tests (week 2). Phase 2: Expand to additional tenants and model classes, enable multi-region failover for read-only workloads (week 3). Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% for designated release, monitor SLOs for 7 days, then promote config to global defaults (week 4). Each phase gated by automated SLO checks and postmortem sign-off. Rollback path: toggle feature flag, revert routing table to previous variant, and run forced cache warm.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for risk score computation and state transitions. - End-to-end simulation harness that replays production traces with injected latency/error faults. - Chaos experiments: region partition, model OOM, GPU preemption. - Load tests validating controlled shedding: measure acceptance rate vs P95/P99 latency. - Integration tests with Console dashboards and alerting rules. - User-visible behavior validated with synthetic cohort in sandbox tenant.
